hero.source: Keramat Iskandar Syah, Fort Canning Park, Singapore - 20110924
hero.description: Keramat Iskandar Syah in Fort Canning Park, Singapore. A keramat is a traditional burial ground of a revered Malay leader. Although this keramat is named after Iskandar Syah (or Shah), another name for Parameswara (1344–1414) who was the last king of Singapura, this could not have been his tomb as he died in Malacca. It is thus not known exactly who is buried here.

gallery.artist: Jon Callas from San Jose, California, USA.
gallery.description: 14th-century gold armlets and rings in East Javanese style, found at Fort Canning Hill, Singapore, in 1928. Displayed in the Singapore History Gallery of the National Museum of Singapore, they were collectively designated by the Museum as one of 11 "national treasures" in January 2006 and by the National Heritage Board as one of the top 12 artefacts held in the collections of its museums. See (1) Lim Wei Chean (31 January 2006). "Singapore's treasures". The Straits Times. (2) Our top twelve artefacts. National Heritage Board. Archived from the original on 2008-08-22. Retrieved on 2007-07-17.
categories: Collection of the Singapore History Gallery, National Museum of Singapore

Fort Canning Park was once the burial ground of Malay kings.

gallery.filename: Statue of Sang Nila Utama at the Raffles Landing Site (front view).jpg
gallery.title: File:Statue of Sang Nila Utama at the Raffles Landing Site (front view).jpg
gallery.source: Statue of Sang Nila Utama at the Raffles Landing Site (front view)
gallery.description:
Statue of en:Sang Nila Utama, a pseudo-legendary Prince from  en:Palembang who supposedly founded the en:Kingdom of Singapura in 1299, erected at the en:Raffles Landing Site as part of events commemorating the bicentennial of Singapore's colonisation by the en:British East India Company at the hands of Sir en:Sir Stamford Raffles.
Full-length front view, with office towers at en:Raffles Place in the background, along with a statue (also erected as part of the bicentennial commemorations) of en:Munshi Abdullah, a Malay linguist in the employ of Sir Stamford Raffles who would come to be known as the "Father of Modern Malay Literature".
